doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Playing in Europe and radio bands
summary: He played with Dexter Gordon, Johnny Griffin, Kenny Clarke and European radio bands, subsidized for jazz, and was treated very well.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Sometimes with American musicians, sometime with European musicians. I played with Dexter Gordon, Johnny Griffin, Benny Bailey, oh just a host of guys that were living — Kenny Clarke. All the guys that were living over there and also with the European musicians. We made radio shows. Because see in every city in Europe there’s a radio band that is subsidized by the government to play a certain amount of jazz every year.

That money — they can only use that money for jazz projects. And they have that same subsidy for classical music and for folk music. So we had a lot of radio shows and television shows and cultural houses where we were playing concerts and festivals and all that. So it was really a fantastic experience.
And you were treated pretty darn well then.
Treated really — I never had that kind of treatment before. It was a surprise to me.
